text:
sam: running into a few odd DX things on Windows + py3.11/3.12 while trying to get the python sample app to run. feels like event loop + TLS + retry semantics + typing are all fighting each other. anyone seen this combo?

sam: repro (Win11, py3.12, fresh venv):
```
> pip install redwood-sdk[async] certifi
> python sample_win.py

# sample_win.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=...) as c:
        await c.generate("hello")

asyncio.run(main())
```

sam: runtime output: first an SSL cert verify error:
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
redwood.errors.NetworkError: TLS handshake failed
```

sam: then my service-layer logs show repeated token refresh attempts (we call the SDK in a background job) and the SDK's retryer keeps retrying the NetworkError, which causes 3 auth refreshes in ~6s.

anya: two separate surfaces here: 1) Windows/OpenSSL cert path on 3.12 can be different, certifi not always auto-used. 2) event loop behavior on Windows sometimes breaks libraries that spawn background tasks if the loop policy differs (Proactor vs Selector).

frank: agreed. one quick test: run `python -c "import ssl, certifi; print(certifi.where(), ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"` and see what PEM is used. if your OpenSSL isn't picking up certifi, constructing transport with `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())` fixes it.

anya: also for event loop: if your app uses some sync code that calls `asyncio.run()` while other threads are using `asyncio` you can see "Event loop is closed" on shutdown. on Windows try setting `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())` before creating loops to mirror Linux behavior for 3rd-party libs that assume selector loops.

sam: interesting — i'm calling into the SDK from a ThreadPoolExecutor worker that itself calls `asyncio.run(...)`. maybe that's the nested loop smell.

frank: additional DX bug: our retry classifier currently treats redwood.errors.NetworkError as retryable by default. when the cause is an ssl.SSLCertVerificationError that's not transient — should be non-retryable and surfaced as a TLSError so callers don't flood auth. propose: add a TLSError subclass that carries the original ssl exception and mark it non-retryable.

sam: +1. that will avoid my background worker repeatedly refreshing tokens.

doc-bot: CI job 6123: windows-integration/test_sample_win.py failed (TLS verify) — https://ci.internal/jobs/6123 (logs attached)

frank: possible SDK code change (small): in transport init do something like:
```python
import platform, ssl, certifi
if platform.system() == "Windows" or os.environ.get("REDWOOD_FORCE_CERTIFI"):
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
else:
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
```
this makes the Windows path deterministic. would also add a minimal unit test that runs on the Windows CI runner.

anya: for typing/async context manager: mypy complains `AsyncClient` has no `__aenter__`/`__aexit__`. simplest fix: implement the dunders on AsyncClient and add `from typing import AsyncContextManager` to the class signature or inherit `typing.AsyncContextManager["AsyncClient"]`. also add a test that `mypy --package redwood` runs in the SDK CI matrix.

sam: i tried `SSL_CERT_FILE` env and it had no effect — looks like OpenSSL build on this runtime prefers Windows cert store unless cafile explicitly supplied.

frank: yeah. that's why the cafile override is safest. also we should ensure exception chaining: raise TLSError("tls failed") from original_ssl_exc so tracebacks keep the root cause.

sam: thanks — that would make my logs much clearer. i'll validate a patch if you open one.

build-bot: created issue #1342: "windows: event loop + TLS + retrying auth on py3.12" assigned to @frank. PR stub referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1299

frank: i'll draft PR with three bits: 1) transport uses certifi on Windows (opt-in via env), 2) TLSError type that preserves ssl error & is marked non-retryable in the retryer, 3) add AsyncClient dunder methods for proper typing and context manager behavior. will add Windows CI test and mypy run.

sam: perfect — also please add a short paragraph to devex docs about common Windows pitfalls (event loop policy + certs + how to set SSL_CERT_FILE in cmd/powershell). that'll save folks time.

anya: one more note: recommend we add a troubleshooting snippet in the SDK README with the two live-check commands: `python -c "import ssl, certifi; print(certifi.where(), ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"` and `python -c "import sys, ssl; print(sys.version, ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)"` so folks can paste into issues.
